title: Password Hashing, Sessions & Tokens
objectives: Hash passwords with salted, slow KDFs (argon2/bcrypt)
Trade off server sessions vs stateless JWTs
Rotate refresh tokens and invalidate sessions

examples.name: hashing.rs

exercise.prompt: Evaluate auth choices: "JWT with 24h expiry, no revocation" (stale-token risk), "short-lived access + rotating refresh" (good), "passwords hashed with SHA-256" (too fast), "argon2 with per-user salt" (good).
hints: Stateless tokens cannot be revoked before expiry — keep them short.
Password hashing must be slow and salted per user.

questions.prompt: Password hashing needs a slow, salted KDF because…
options: fast hashes let attackers brute-force billions of guesses cheaply
questions.explanation: argon2/bcrypt burn CPU per guess; per-user salts kill precomputation.

options: statelessness (no lookup, no revocation) vs session control
questions.explanation: Stateless tokens scale but cannot be revoked before expiry; sessions invert that.
